page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the ARMv8 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs utilizing the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography.

Benchmark results indicate modest performance characteristics. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is average at 1812.29, and single-threaded gzip compression reaches 24.01 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is weak at 3594.57, and the Geekbench multi-core score is poor at 1997.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block performance at 26.99 GB/sec and write large block performance at 16.42 GB/sec. Passmark database operations score at 1416.76, while static web serving throughput is measured at 2.66 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-2 offers a low-cost entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, utilizing a resource-dense architecture with dedicated physical cores rather than hyperthreaded virtual cores. Due to its modest multi-core performance and limited memory bandwidth, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and simple text processing tasks that do not require high-performance computing or extensive memory capacity.
